DraftKings odds and player props, from ESPN

Source: R/espn.R
espn_odds.Rd

ESPN's NHL odds come from DraftKings, and its APIs (unlike DraftKings' own, which refuse requests from servers) are open:

Usage

espn_odds(date = NULL)

espn_props(date = NULL, nhl_ids = TRUE)

Arguments

date

A date (or "YYYY-MM-DD"); NULL for today.

nhl_ids

Add each player's NHL id (four more requests a game).

Value

A tibble.

Details

  • espn_odds(): every game's moneyline, puck line and total, opening and current, with the no-vig chance of each side.

  • espn_props(): DraftKings' player props for a day's games, about 500 a game: shots on goal, points, assists, saves, anytime and first goalscorer, the "2+ shots" style milestones, power-play points, and each club's goal total. Each over/under comes as one row with both prices. With nhl_ids = TRUE every player gets his NHL id, for joining to the rest of the package.

ESPN lists an over/under as two entries without naming the sides, over first: in every pair checked against the same player's milestone prices (October 2026), the first entry was the over. Players come as ESPN ids and are matched to NHL rosters by club, sweater number and surname, then by name. ESPN drops a game's odds once it starts.

See also

devig() for the no-vig chance of any pair of prices.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
espn_odds()
props <- espn_props()
props[props$market == "Total Shots on Goal", c("player_name", "team", "line", "over", "under")]
}
